en.headline: Buildings Department orders checks on eight more houses at One Stanley
en.dek: The developer updated its sales brochure after the department required investigations of additional detached houses following earlier rebar irregularities.
body: The Buildings Department has ordered the developer of the One Stanley luxury estate in Stanley to investigate eight further detached houses, common areas of one block, and the original house where steel reinforcement irregularities were found, according to an updated sales brochure released on Friday.

The department’s letter, dated 2 October, required the developer to submit findings within one month. The additional houses listed are numbers 5, 8, 16, 17, 19, 32, 33 and 36. Half of those houses have already been sold, the developer said.

Earlier inspections of the original house had shown that the concrete cover of a ground-floor beam lacked required wire mesh and that some floor-slab reinforcement did not match approved plans. The department has said the overall structure posed no obvious danger but that work quality warranted concern.
The developer previously offered a six-year structural warranty and free independent inspections to owners and buyers amid the probe.

zh.headline: 屋宇署要求One Stanley再查八座獨立屋鋼筋問題
zh.dek: 發展商更新售樓書，披露屋宇署於十月二日要求就另外八座洋房及公用地方進行調查，一個月內提交報告。
body: 赤柱豪宅One Stanley發展商周五更新售樓書，披露屋宇署已要求就另外八座獨立屋、第九座公用地方及原涉事單位進行調查，並於一個月內提交報告。
根據十月二日的通知，需要調查的獨立屋包括5、8、16、17、19、32、33及36號。發展商表示，新要求調查的八座中半數已出售，並已與相關買家溝通。
較早前屋宇署發現原涉事單位地面一條橫樑混凝土保護層未按圖則配置鋼絲網，部分樓板鋼筋配置亦與圖則不符。署方指整體結構未構成明顯危險，但施工質素值得關注。
發展商此前已提出向業主及買家提供額外六年結構保養及免費獨立檢測。
